q: Who is known as the father of Indian Planning?
exp: Sir M. Visvesvaraya is called the father of Indian Planning for his early blueprint (1934). Answer: M. Visvesvaraya

q: The Reserve Bank of India was established in which year?
exp: The RBI was established on 1 April 1935 under the RBI Act, 1934. Answer: 1935

q: GST was introduced in India on which date?
exp: The Goods and Services Tax (GST) was implemented on 1 July 2017. Answer: 1 July 2017

q: NITI Aayog replaced which body as the government's policy think tank?
exp: NITI Aayog (2015) replaced the Planning Commission (1950). Answer: Planning Commission

q: Which sector contributes the largest share to India's GDP (services sector)?
exp: The services (tertiary) sector contributes the largest share (over 50%) to India's GDP. Answer: Services

q: The first Five Year Plan of India focused mainly on which sector?
exp: The first Five Year Plan (1951–56) focused on agriculture and irrigation (Harrod-Domar model). Answer: Agriculture

q: Repo rate is the rate at which?
exp: Repo rate is the rate at which the RBI lends short-term funds to commercial banks. Answer: RBI lends to commercial banks

q: The 'Green Revolution' in India is associated with which crops?
exp: The Green Revolution (1960s) dramatically increased wheat and rice production. Answer: Wheat and rice

q: Who is the author of the book 'Poor Economics' associated with Indian economist Abhijit Banerjee?
exp: 'Poor Economics' (2011) was written by Abhijit V. Banerjee and Esther Duflo. Answer: Abhijit Banerjee and Esther Duflo

q: The headquarters of the Reserve Bank of India is located in?
exp: The RBI headquarters is in Mumbai. Answer: Mumbai

Deficit in the balance of payments
exp: Fiscal deficit = total expenditure − total receipts excluding borrowings. Answer: Total expenditure minus total receipts excluding borrowings

q: Which organisation releases the Consumer Price Index (CPI) based inflation data in India?
exp: The NSO (under MoSPI) releases CPI data; RBI uses it for inflation targeting. Answer: National Statistical Office (NSO)

q: The Minimum Support Price (MSP) is recommended by which body?
opts: Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP)
exp: The CACP recommends MSPs for major crops; the Cabinet Committee decides. Answer: Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP)

q: 'Demonetisation' of high-value currency notes was announced in India on which date?
exp: The demonetisation of ₹500 and ₹1000 notes was announced on 8 November 2016. Answer: 8 November 2016

q: The 'Blue Revolution' in India refers to the development of which sector?
exp: The Blue Revolution refers to rapid growth of fish production/aquaculture. Answer: Fisheries and aquaculture
